title: Landscape crop diversity and semi-natural habitat affect crop pollinators, pollination benefit and yield
decision_basis: Primary study uses landscape crop diversity and semi-natural habitat as predictors of pollinator density/foraging behaviour including robbery; it does not test floral or visitor-flower access geometry as the robbery predictor.
notes: Route-resolved foraging behaviour is measured, but the focal predictor is landscape context rather than access geometry.

title: Landscape complexity benefits bumble bee visitation in faba bean (Vicia faba minor L.) but crop productivity is not pollinator-dependent
decision_basis: Primary study monitors legitimate visitation, nectar robbing and extrafloral visitation across a landscape-complexity gradient in one faba-bean cultivar; no access-geometry predictor is tested against robbery.
notes: Landscape context predicts foraging behaviour, outside the frozen geometry-to-route contract.

title: Pollination mutualisms in Caryophyllaceae
decision_basis: Source is a New Phytologist Forum commentary synthesizing papers in a feature issue rather than an independent empirical study program.
notes: Secondary/commentary document excluded from the formal direct-study denominator.

title: Biting the hand that feeds you: wedge-billed hummingbird is a nectar robber of a sicklebill-adapted Andean bellflower
decision_basis: Natural-history report supports a mechanical-mismatch interpretation of robbery on a sicklebill-adapted flower, but does not provide the required quantitative comparison/model of access geometry against robbery route probability/frequency.

title: Corolla Abscission Triggered by Nectar Robbers Positively Affects Reproduction by Enhancing Self-Pollination in Symphytum officinale (Boraginaceae)
decision_basis: Primary question is how nectar robbery triggers corolla abscission and alters reproduction; robbery is the antecedent treatment/state rather than a route outcome predicted by independently measured access geometry.

title: Corolla stickiness prevents nectar robbing in Erica
decision_basis: Primary anti-robbery predictor is experimentally manipulated floral stickiness/adhesive strength. Corolla length/shape are analyzed as correlates of stickiness, not as the focal predictor of robbery outcome.
notes: Important floral-defence evidence, but outside the frozen access-geometry direct-test lane.

title: Morphological specialisation for primary nectar robbing in a pollen specialist mining bee (Hymenoptera, Andrenidae)
decision_basis: Study documents specialized bee morphology and primary nectar-robbing behaviour, but does not estimate a quantitative relation between variation in an access-geometry variable and robbery probability/frequency across independent units.
notes: Morphological adaptation evidence is contextual, not a codable direct geometry-to-route test.

title: Trait matching affects the probability of nectar robbing in plant-pollinator networks
decision_basis: Dryad record is a data/repository object for the Aubert_Duchenne standardized-network program rather than an independent primary study report.
notes: Primary biological program already represented in the standardized network; repository object cannot add a formal direct-study denominator unit.

title: Data from: Bird extinctions shift bill-flower trait matching in Hawaiian lobelioids
decision_basis: Dryad record is the data object for the Case et al. Hawaiian lobelioid study, not an independent biological study program.
notes: Primary Case program is already coded separately; data object excluded.

title: Data from: Is bee-avoidance by bird-pollinated flowers driven by nectar robbing in Erica?
decision_basis: Dryad record is a repository data object and cannot constitute an independent primary direct-test program.
notes: Primary article, if eligible, must be adjudicated separately.
